title: "Labs"
subtitle: "Hands-on time series analysis in R"
toc: false
---

The lectures argue; the labs make you do it. Each one is a complete Quarto
document — open the `.qmd`, run it chunk by chunk, then change something and see
what breaks. Data comes from the `data/` folder or is pulled live from SBP, PBS,
Yahoo Finance and the World Bank.

## New to R?

Start here before the method labs. These four sessions take you from installing
R to writing tidyverse pipelines confidently.

::: {.card-grid}
<a class="tcard" href="r-foundations/r-01-getting-started.html">
  <span class="num">R 1</span><span class="ttl">Learn the basics of R</span>
  <span class="dsc">Installation, the Positron/RStudio interface, objects, vectors and your first plot.</span></a>
<a class="tcard" href="r-foundations/r-02-r-fundamentals.html">
  <span class="num">R 2</span><span class="ttl">R fundamentals, extended</span>
  <span class="dsc">Data types, subsetting, functions and reading files of every awkward format.</span></a>
<a class="tcard" href="r-foundations/r-03-tidyverse-day-1.html">
  <span class="num">R 3</span><span class="ttl">Tidyverse, day one</span>
  <span class="dsc">filter, select, mutate, group_by and summarise — the five verbs that do most of the work.</span></a>
<a class="tcard" href="r-foundations/r-04-tidyverse-in-action.html">
  <span class="num">R 4</span><span class="ttl">Tidyverse in action</span>
  <span class="dsc">A full analysis end to end: import, tidy, model, visualise, communicate.</span></a>
:::

Applied case studies that go beyond the teaching sequence — remittances,
exports, tax revenue, solar prices — live in the `applications/` folder of the
[repository](https://github.com/Zahedasghar/timeseries).
